datums.C: 3× Ø8 posts on Ø76 PCD at 120° (tertiary). Locates the top plate. Wings sit in the bays between posts.

fits_mm.location_posts_plate: +0.40 diametral (Ø8.0 / Ø8.4), posts through the plate
fits_mm.location_bushing_seat: +0.40 diametral (Ø14.0 / Ø14.4) with a 2 mm land
fits_mm.wing_tenon_hub_socket: +0.40 width (7.6 / 8.0); 0.20 axial float in a 5 mm pocket
fits_mm.centering_cone: 0.20 radial at the cup mouth (male r 4.8 in female r 5.0)
fits_mm.axial_thrust_and_cap: 0.20 float — running faces do not occupy the same volume

gdt.position: Post and wing-socket patterns positional Ø0.4 MMC to B (one nozzle). FDM cannot hold tighter without a gauge print.

lessons.title: Clearance is a design input
lessons.teach: A 0.4 mm Bambu nozzle cannot hold CNC fits. Model +0.40 mm diametral clearance in CAD for every printed-to-printed running or slip interface, including the wing tenon in the hub socket. Leave slicer XY hole compensation at 0 unless a gauge print says otherwise.

lessons.title: No FDM press fits
lessons.teach: Press fits fail from elephant foot and shrinkage. Use +0.40 slip and retain with a shoulder, land, plate, or cap. The wing drops into a socket; it is not a press. Do not assume a metal bearing will appear later.

lessons.title: The wing uses the frame
lessons.teach: The frame is a two-bearing stand: cup in the base, sleeve in the top plate, posts through the plate. The hub sits on the shoulder and carries three sockets. Each wing drops a tenon into a socket and sweeps a bay between the posts. Assembly order: base → shaft → hub → three wings → top plate → bushing → cap.

lessons.title: Print a thrust bearing that can actually spin
lessons.teach: A lifted same-angle cone never touches (parallel surfaces). Center with a 45° cup and a smaller male cone, and take thrust on a narrow annular land with 0.20 mm float. Relief under the apex so the tip does not bottom.

lessons.title: Keep the machine even
lessons.teach: Three posts at 120° and three wings at 120° in the bays between them (60° offset). Double-D so the hub turns the shaft. An odd one-sided vane is not a turbine.

lessons.title: Prefer printed bushings
lessons.teach: Printed cone + land for thrust, printed sleeve in a shouldered top plate for radial. Plate thicker than the bushing so the seat has a land. Prefer bushings over roller/ball bearings at this size. Metal 608 / catalog bearings are a later table, not a hidden part.

lessons.title: The wing is a part that mounts
lessons.teach: A leftover helical C-loft is not a wing. A concentric ring sector is not a wing. A flat plate is a vane, not an airfoil. The wing is a named symmetric section (NACA 0021 or the 2026 0024–4.5/3.5 family), chord tangential, span up the bay, tenon into the hub. Windows in the top plate keep the blades visible.

lessons.title: The section is a 2026-appropriate airfoil
lessons.teach: Directionless VAWTs see reversing α. Build a thick symmetric airfoil (t/c 21–24%, blunt TE ≥ 2 nozzles). Cite the section. A hoop or a rectangle of the same bbox is a fail even if the stack spins.

lessons.title: Publish the design report
lessons.teach: Write the iteration log, the design process (airfoil, Re, fits, finish, bushings), the final BOM, and plastic/material cost (volume × density × $/kg). READY TO PRINT without a costed report is a fail.

lessons.title: Export a printable package
lessons.teach: Assign appearances, run solid_export_preflight, then solid_export_3mf for bambu_studio. Print each body in its own orientation (base/plate flat, shaft on the land, bushing as a ring, hub on its face, wings standing so layer lines run spanwise). 3MF is the manufacturing handoff.
